result:
The 30-minute lesson on O3 is written, with a quiz and a cheat sheet to go with it.

**Lesson:** `lessons/0001-context-and-memory-in-an-agent.html`. It starts with a recall warm-up on the agent loop. Then it covers:
- **Context window:** what the model sees on one call, shown with the makerspace assistant.
- **Between steps:** the model keeps nothing, and the program re-sends the whole history every call. A worked cost table shows why one large tool result is paid for again on every later call.
- **Context getting too full:** context rot, clearing old tool results and compaction.
- **Between sessions:** notes versus a database for training status.
- **Retrieval:** chunks, embeddings and keyword search. It also gives the rule that you can skip retrieval if the manuals fit in the prompt.

It ends with a worked placement exercise for deciding where each piece of information goes, a faded exercise, and a summary. The win is that you can place each piece of information in context, notes or database, or retrieval.

The main source is Anthropic's [Effective context engineering for AI agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents). I also used the Claude docs on context windows and Anthropic's Contextual Retrieval post. All three are in `RESOURCES.md`.

**Also written:**
- Quiz 0002 (five items) and its key; ask me for it when you want to take it.
- `cheatsheets/0001-context-and-memory.html`, a one-page "where does it go?" table.
- `NOTES.md`, updated. I also noted that quiz 0001 is still ungraded.

The token counts in the lesson's tables are made-up illustrative numbers, and the lesson says so. I haven't checked the lesson's word count with a tool; I estimate about 3,700 words, inside the 2,700–6,750 range.

I didn't write a learning record, since you haven't yet shown understanding of this material. In the lesson's warm-up, you're asked to guess what "token" and "context window" limit. Send me your guess in the chat and I'll tell you how close it is.
